etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ago, agon (“passed”), past participle of agon (“to depart, escape, pass”), from Old English āgān (“to go away, pass away, go forth, come to pass”), from Proto-Germanic *uz- (“out”), *gāną (“to go”), equivalent to a- +‎ gone, and by surface analysis, a- +‎ go. Cognate with German ergehen (“to come to pass, fare, go forth”). Compare also Old Saxon āgangan (“to go or pass by”), Gothic 𐌿𐍃𐌲𐌰𐌲𐌲𐌰𐌽 (usgaggan, “to go forth”).

definitions.definition: (archaic or dialectal) Gone; gone by; gone away; passed; passed away.
(archaic or dialectal) Nearly gone; dead. (used in Devonshire at the turn of the 19th century)

quote.citation: 2013 August 10, “Damned if you don’t”, in The Economist, volume 408, number 8848:
quote.text: Two years ago a pair of scientists sparked fears of a devastating virus.
